actions.findings:
Operational causal memory requires a persistent state to facilitate information transfer over time, which is strictly bounded by the accessibility of the underlying Markovian description. [source-6b1bb6af50ef4e9b] [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

Coarse-graining of physical dynamics imposes a fundamental limit on the objectivity of persistent memory, as it hides the microscopic process producing the observable state. [source-ee8169aea35a4ece] [peer-42ea5272a464585193f493cc]
actions.limitations: Existing models predominantly assume overdamped or Markovian dynamics. The mapping of these operational definitions to non-Markovian memory architectures remains under-constrained.
actions.next_questions: How does the precision of predictive control scale with the thermodynamic cost of maintaining specific internal pointer states in non-Markovian environments?
actions.reason: Revision to integrate coarse-graining limits on causal inference and predictive sufficiency.
actions.summary: Physical memory functions as an operational causal state when internal degrees of freedom enable predictive control over future system dynamics. This relationship is fundamentally limited by coarse-graining, which restricts access to exact Markovian trajectories and necessitates lower-bound inference on entropy production.
